evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system Jira (ACME), Git source GitHub (acme), Default branch develop, Commit policy PRs never direct, Commit convention conventional w/ scope + ticket ref in PR body only, CI watcher CircleCI, PR shape draft-first squash CODEOWNERS review, Remote yes. Open a PR for my changes on feat/composition-panel — no linked ticket yet.
evals.expected_output: The widgets-like path, unchanged in behaviour: inspect, one batched Gate 1 (ticket, branch target, split, review), a plan with atomic conventional-scope commits and a template-based description, Gate 2, then a draft PR and a hand-off line naming the CI watch.
assertions: Reads the workflow profile rows from context before asking anything
Runs the git inspection (branch, base develop, status, diff, branch lead) first
Asks about the ticket because Ticket system names a tracker, detecting the id through the profile's Tracker rules detection order
Commits nothing and pushes nothing before Gate 2 approval
Uses conventional commit subjects with a scope and no ticket id, putting the reference in the PR body only, as the Commit convention row says
Creates the PR with --draft because the PR shape row is draft-first
Closes by saying a hook hands off to the CI watch, since the CI watcher row names CircleCI
Names no other skill anywhere in the run

evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system none, Git source GitHub (acme), Default branch main, Commit policy direct commits to main, Commit convention conventional w/ scope, CI watcher none, PR shape n/a, Remote yes. Commit and PR this.
evals.expected_output: Under direct commits to main it commits on the default branch and stops: no branch, no PR, no ticket question, and it says plainly that no CI watch follows.
assertions: Honors Commit policy direct commits to main — commits on main with no branch created and no PR opened
Asks no ticket question and performs no tracker move, because Ticket system is none
Still splits the work into atomic conventional-scope commits, one per concern, gated at Gate 2
Drafts no PR description
Says plainly that no CI watch follows, since the CI watcher row is none
Explains the direct-commit choice rather than silently ignoring the PR half of the request

evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system none, Git source none, Default branch main, Commit policy PRs never direct, Commit convention conventional w/ scope, CI watcher none, PR shape n/a, Remote local-only. Ship these changes.
evals.expected_output: With Remote local-only the run ends at the commits: it builds the split, gates it, commits, and reports that nothing was pushed and no PR exists to open.
assertions: Stops at the commits because Remote is local-only — no git push and no gh pr create
Reports explicitly that nothing was pushed rather than failing on a missing remote
Skips the branch-target question that only applies to a remote PR flow
Asks no ticket question and says no CI watch follows

evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system Jira (ACME), Default branch develop, Commit policy PRs never direct, Commit convention conventional w/ scope + ticket ref in PR body only, CI watcher CircleCI, PR shape draft-first squash CODEOWNERS review, Remote yes, Reviewers claude and codex. The approved plan is in context: its Closing steps line reads 'review: judgment tier x 2' and it prescribes two commits. Cut the PR for ACME-2258.
evals.expected_output: It takes the tier and the count from the plan's Closing steps line, delegates to the review capability read-only, applies the findings it accepts itself and re-reads the diff, follows the plan's prescribed commit split, and asks the tracker move batched into Gate 2.
assertions: Reads the tier and reviewer count from the plan's Closing steps review line rather than offering its own
Delegates to the review capability with exactly that tier and count
Treats reviewers as read-only — the main agent applies the accepted findings and no reviewer edits the tree
Re-reads the working-tree diff after applying the accepted fixes, before building the split and the description
Follows the commit split the plan prescribed instead of regrouping by its own analysis
Batches the move of ACME-2258 to the work-started state into the Gate 2 interaction, best-effort on failure
Adds an Agent review section to the PR body naming coverage, findings, verdict, and which findings were applied

evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system Jira (ACME), Default branch develop, Commit policy PRs never direct, CI watcher CircleCI, PR shape draft-first squash CODEOWNERS review, Remote yes. Commit and PR this — the diff mixes a bugfix and an unrelated refactor. Split them.
evals.expected_output: Detects the two concerns, confirms the split at Gate 1, then runs the build-and-execute steps once per concern, presenting all per-concern plans at a single Gate 2, with the tracker move running once up front.
assertions: Detects the two concerns from the diff and asks whether to proceed as one PR or split
Produces one branch, its atomic commits, and one PR per concern
Presents the per-concern plans together at a single Gate 2
Runs the tracker move once up front for the single ticket, not once per PR
Bases each concern's branch per the Gate 1 choice — independent off develop, or stacked

evals.prompt: Profile: Ticket system Jira (ACME), Default branch develop, Commit policy PRs never direct, CI watcher GitHub Actions, PR shape squash CODEOWNERS review, Remote yes. Update the existing PR for this branch with my new commits. It already has a description I wrote by hand.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the non-template body, warns at Gate 2 that it would be replaced and offers to keep it, and on approval pushes and updates via gh pr edit; with a PR shape that is not draft-first it opens nothing as a draft, and it still hands off to the CI watch.
assertions: Detects the existing PR and that its body is non-template
Warns at Gate 2 that the hand-written body would be replaced and offers to keep it
Replaces the body only on explicit approval, via gh pr edit --body-file -
Omits --draft because the PR shape row is not draft-first
Never promotes the PR to ready, merges it, or watches CI itself, closing instead on the hand-off to the CI watch
Aborts a hunk-level commit cleanly on a git apply --cached failure, pushing no partial result
